Subject: Production latency spike + 502/503s after Friday config roll

Hi Marissa / Laura,

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency on our BrightHarbor private cluster at ~02:00 UTC this morning following the config change your team applied on Friday night (v2026.11.06-configA).

Symptoms:
- p50 unchanged, p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~3.6s, p99 to ~7.8s.
- Error rate for model endpoint "bh-retrieval-v2" elevated to 4.1% (mainly 502/503).
- Throughput is steady but we see batches queuing on the gateway leading to head-of-line waits.
- Observed spikes coincide with large multi-turn requests from a partner set.

We attached a small log snippet with request ids and stack traces (error_snippet.txt).

This is customer-impacting — our ops team has traffic-shed to a fallback but we need a remediation plan and a timeline. We are tracking this as a P1 with our execs breathing down us.

Immediate asks:
1) Can Redwood flip the route to the fallback model variant from your side while we validate?
2) Any quick config rollback or throttling knobs you recommend?
3) ETA for a deeper root-cause analysis and patch?

Sanjay
Director of ML Ops
BrightHarbor.ai

Subject: Re: Production latency spike + 502/503s after Friday config roll

Marissa / Laura / Sanjay — quick technical update from the first-pass triage.

What we see:
- KV cache growth on the bh-retrieval service — the in-memory prefix KV store is not trimming fast enough after the config change that raised the cache window. Cache size growth triggers more swapping behavior on the node and increases GC pauses; this disproportionately affects p95/p99.
- A second issue: background async prefetch workers are failing intermittently due to an edge-case in our LZ4 decompression path when payloads exceed 1.2MB (probable regression introduced in the Friday build). Failures surface as 502s and cause request retries which amplify the queue.

Proposed remediation (safe order):
1) Immediately flip traffic to fallback model variant (Marissa already suggested) — low-risk and reverses pressure.
2) Apply a temporary kv_trim policy to reduce effective cache size to 0.6x on BrightHarbor hosts (config toggle) — non-disruptive and reversible.
3) Disable async prefetch for heavy multi-turn sessions as a short-term workaround.
4) Push a small hotfix to the decompression path (we've prepared a patch) and test in staging for 30m. Patch file: kv_cache_patch.patch.

I can get the kv_trim toggle applied within 15 minutes if BrightHarbor approves. For the patch, estimate 3 hours for staging test + 1 hour for rollout assuming no regressions.

I'll open JIRA INF-9482 to track the work and post logs.

Jonas Weber
Sr. SW Eng, Inference Runtime
